# Development {#sec-development}

This chapter covers build, release, and the project conventions.
Testing has its own chapter.

## Build

Check the project with pedantic mode:

```bash
hemtt check -p -e
```

Pedantic mode treats warnings as errors. Build the PBOs with:

```bash
hemtt build
```

Make a release with:

```bash
hemtt release
```

Release signs the PBOs with a per-release key and makes the bikey and zip
files. No private key is required or stored.

## Continuous integration

GitHub Actions runs these checks on every push:

- `hemtt check -p -e`
- `hemtt build`
- The Python validators and physics tests
- An SBOM on release tags
- Release-drafter

The Docker test runs nightly and on demand. The nightly run executes on a
self-hosted runner that already holds an Arma 3 dedicated server, so no
server download is needed. The operator registers that runner once, with
the labels `self-hosted`, `linux` and `aee`, and sets the repository
variable `ARMA3_SERVER_ROOT`.

## Conventions

### Naming

Functions use the name `aee_<component>_fnc_<name>`. PBOs use the name
`aee_<component>`. Shared state uses `aee_core_*` mission variables.

Each function file is `functions/fnc_<name>.sqf`. The files are registered in
`XEH_PREP.hpp` and compiled through CBA XEH. This is the standard `ACE3`/`CBA`
pattern.

Localisation uses a per-addon `stringtable.xml`. Keys use the form
`STR_AEE_<Component>_<Key>`.

### Shared state reads

State is read from `missionNamespace` with `QGVAR`/`QEGVAR` keys. Every
read must type-guard against a missing or garbage value - an unguarded
`getVariable [key, 0]` fallback is the #154 bug class (a nil read that
a code path treats as "gate off", silently disabling a system).

Use `aee_core_fnc_readState` for the guarded read:

```sqf
private _heat = [QGVAR(barrelHeat), 0.3, 1, true] call EFUNC(core,readState);
```

Arguments: key, default, type (0 any / 1 number / 2 string / 3 array /
4 bool), and the `_neverZero` flag. Pass `true` for the last argument
when the value is a GATE - a 0 result is replaced by the default so a
missing state cannot silently kill the system it gates.

### Per-frame cache convention

An expensive per-frame read (eye position, illuminance, smoothed
weather) is computed once per frame and cached by `diag_frameNo`, with
N consumers reading the cached value. The `getEyeState` and
`getSmoothedWeather` functions are the models:

```sqf
private _frame = diag_frameNo;
private _cache = missionNamespace getVariable [QGVAR(cacheName), []];
if (count _cache >= 2 && {(_cache select 0) == _frame}) exitWith {
    _cache select 1
};
// ... compute ...
missionNamespace setVariable [QGVAR(cacheName), [_frame, _result]];
_result
```

New systems that read an expensive state once per frame should follow
this pattern instead of recomputing per consumer.

### Settings

AEE registers its settings at mission start with `CBA_fnc_addSetting`. Each
addon registers its own settings from `addons/<component>/initSettings.inc.sqf`,
included from that addon's `XEH_preInit.sqf`. The framework settings appear
under the **AEE** category. Each module registers under an **AEE <Component>**
category.

### EDEN module

The EDEN module, AEE Environment Config, is placed by mission editors. The
module is global. It exposes these fields:

- `biomeOverride`
- `tempOffset`
- `precipBias`
- `windMultiplier`
- `updateInterval`

### Contributing

The project uses trunk-based development. All commits must be signed. A
pre-commit hook runs `hemtt check -p -e`, `ste-lint`, and `audit`.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/lErrorl404l/AEE/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the full guide.

### Verify techniques against workshop source, not only the wiki

The BIS wiki is incomplete for some scripting topics. It marks the
`DepthOfField` post-process effect as "TBD" with no parameter table, and
states `camSetFocus` works only on `camCreate` cameras. Both are true of
the wiki, but the first is misleading: production workshop mods use
`DepthOfField` in the player view with `ppEffectForceInNVG true`.

The lesson: before declaring a rendering or scripting feature
impossible, search the Steam Workshop for a mod that does it and read its
source. Real implementations beat a wiki placeholder every time. TFN NVG
Effects (workshop 3682613859) proved the NVG depth-of-field technique
that this project now uses. KtweaK's NVG (workshop 3711042620) shows a
distance-based dynamicBlur alternative.

Technique sources referenced in this project:

| Feature | Workshop reference | Technique |
|---|---|---|
| NVG depth of field | TFN NVG Effects (3682613859) | `DepthOfField` ppEffect, `ppEffectForceInNVG true`, `ppEffectAdjust [blur, dist, 1]` |
| Distance-aware blur | KtweaK's NVG (3711042620) | `dynamicBlur` scaled by range factor |
| Thermal/CC params | A3TI (2041057379) | `DEFAULT_TIPP_SETTINGS` brightness/contrast |

### The aircraft data corpus

The directory `data/aircraft/` holds one sourced entry per real aircraft
variant. It is a sibling of the vehicle corpus and inherits that contract by
reference. The corpus feeds four flight-model inputs: the weight in kg, the
rated power in W, the drag area in m2 and the rotor disc area in m2. The
generated lookup `addons/mobility/functions/fnc_getAircraftData.sqf` reads the
corpus at build time. The kernel
`addons/mobility/functions/fnc_calculateAirEngineLoad.sqf` is not changed.

The runtime defaults 150000 W, 0.7 m2 and 50 m2 are the fallback for an empty
row. A bound class reads a sourced value instead.

To refresh the corpus after a data change, run `tools/build_aircraft_data.sh`.
It validates the corpus, writes the coverage and gap reports, generates the
projection and then checks that the committed files are current. The three
commands it runs are `tools/validation/validate_aircraft_data.py`,
`tools/validation/gen_aircraft_coverage.py` and
`tools/validation/gen_aircraft_data.py`.

The licence rules are facts only. Cite a figure, never vendor a proprietary
document. DTIC and NASA NTRS reports, FAA data sheets and manufacturer
datasheets are held. Jane's and EUROCONTROL BADA are reference-only. A figure
whose only source is unheld is marked UNSOURCED and never fills a runtime
field.

Non-goals: the corpus adds no PBO, no addon and no CBA setting. It reads no
Arma config value as a figure. It does not replace the engine flight model.
